messages:
incident-bot: P1 — Dedicated pool 'dedicated-acme-prod' reports sustained GPU saturation (100%) and long request queue (>2300). Burst tokens depleted. Tenant: ACME-enterprise (VPC). Autoscaler disabled by policy.

maria (oncall): paging @ajay @derek @nina-cs. I'm taking ownership for triage. Is this isolated to ACME's pool or a wider infra issue?

ajay (infra): pulling pool metadata. dedicated-acme-prod: dedicated=true, autoscaler=disabled (org policy: manual approve for enterprise), max_nodes=10, active=10. No spare capacity in us-west-2. Cross-region spare: us-west-1=3, us-east-1=5.

derek (ml-infra): telemetry shows very long-lived streaming sessions from ACME's tenant (avg session duration > 18m) for a specific chat route that pins KV cache and stops eviction. Model is a large attention-heavy variant (gpt-xl-16k). Memory blowouts cause GPUs to stay occupied.

nina-cs: ACME support channel: multiple clients report timeouts and some queued requests failing fast. They want immediate mitigation and confirmation there will be no data commingling.

maria (oncall): mitigation brainstorm: (1) enable cross-region burst and route a subset; (2) apply tenant-scoped throttling on new session creation; (3) spin up quantized/cached variant behind VPC ingress with strict ACLs; (4) temporarily bump non-critical request timeouts so long streams are curtailed. Legal/security check needed before moving any tenant traffic off VPC.

ajay (infra): quick note: ACME's VPC config prevents automatic routing to hosted pool due to data residency rules. We can burst to another dedicated pool in a different region within their VPC if they have one, or request explicit customer opt-in to use hosted fallback. Otherwise our only immediate levers are throttling and manual provisioning.

derek (ml-infra): technical take: spinning new GPUs in the same VPC in us-east-1 takes ~3-5m for node provisioning + ~3m for model warm/kv sync. There is also an option to run a trimmed model on CPU workers inside the VPC as an emergency degradation path (latency >> but preserves isolation).

ops-bot: capacity report: dedicated-acme-prod: nodes=10/10, burst_tokens=0; spare by-region: us-east-1:5, us-west-1:3. VPC-linked dedicated pools available only in us-east-1 (3 nodes).

maria (oncall): propose immediate steps: A) enable per-tenant session-creation throttling to cap new sessions to 10/sec, B) provision 4 nodes in us-east-1 and start draining oldest queued requests there, C) ask CS to request ACME opt-in for hosted fallback if they will allow. Anyone object?

ajay (infra): executing provision in us-east-1. Creating job job-b7c2 with region=us-east-1, add_nodes=4, vpc_attach=true. Kicking off throttling rule now.

derek (ml-infra): note: enabling session throttling will drop some in-flight handoff logic; recommend graceful 429 with Retry-After header and a short backoff guidance. Also starting background KV eviction pass to free memory on existing nodes.

nina-cs: messaging to ACME: "We've enacted emergency throttles and are provisioning additional capacity within your VPC. No data is leaving your VPC. Expect improvements within ~10 minutes. We'll update in 15." They acknowledged but asked for SLA credit assessment.

maria (oncall): handing operational control to ajay at 04:05 UTC to run provisioning and routing. I'll stay for CS coordination. If I go silent, page sre-pager.

ajay (infra): provision command:
```bash
POST https://internal.api.redwood/v1/pools/dedicated-acme-prod/provision
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN
Body: {"add_nodes":4,"region":"us-east-1","vpc_attach":true}
```
Job created: job-b7c2. Monitoring.

ops-bot: job-b7c2 status: provisioning (1/4 ready). model_sync: 20%. KV-eviction started on busy nodes.

derek (ml-infra): starting an emergency CPU-fallback within the VPC as a last resort (cpu-fallback group cg-2) — this will preserve tenant isolation but expect 5-10x latency. Activating only if queue doesn't fall within 8 minutes.

maria (oncall): CS: confirm that CPU-fallback preserves encryption with customer KMS and no keys leave the VPC.

nina-cs: confirmed with security: CPU fallback runs inside VPC, keys remain in tenant KMS; security approves for emergency only. Customer informed.

ops-bot: job-b7c2 update: 4/4 nodes ready; model_sync 78%; KV warm 35%. Queue length decreasing slowly.

ajay (infra): shifting 25% of new sessions to new nodes in us-east-1, keeping older sessions pinned to original nodes to avoid kv transfer churn. Applied traffic rule:
{"pool":"dedicated-acme-prod","split":{"us-east-1-new":"25%","original":"75%"},"session_policy":"pin_existing"}

derek (ml-infra): metrics: queue dropped from 2310 -> 450 over 9 minutes. GPU utilization on original nodes still high due to long streams but new nodes absorbing new sessions. Latency on new nodes stable ~260ms.

sre-pager: logged ticket INC-ACME-244 assigned to ajay for remediation and derek for post-incident analysis. Noted legal check on cross-VPC routing.

maria (oncall): initial mitigation effective. We need next-day remediation: enable tenant-scoped autoscaler with human-in-the-loop approval, implement per-tenant long-session alerting, and add automated pre-warm for known hot models. I'll file follow-ups.

ajay (infra): created remediation change: "tenant-autoscale-proposal for enterprise-acme: enable autoscaler(min=4,max=20) with approval workflow" -> REDW-244-CHG.

derek (ml-infra): post-incident items: 1) add long-session eviction/runbook, 2) build CPU-fallback playbook, 3) KV eviction tuning for gpt-xl-16k, 4) test model-snapshot quick-pull to reduce warm time.

nina-cs: ACME asked for a written timeline and root-cause analysis once available. We'll prepare a customer-facing summary.

ops-bot: incident state -> mitigated (service restored for majority of requests). Monitoring for full stabilization.

maria (oncall): closing active coordination. Current status: mitigated; customer has partial service restored. ETA for remediation tasks: 48h for autoscaler and runbooks. Handoff: ajay continues remediation; derek to lead postmortem. If regressions, page sre-pager.
summary: Dedicated ACME VPC pool saturated by long-lived streaming sessions causing KV retention and GPU pinning. Mitigation: tenant session throttling, provisioned 4 VPC-attached nodes in us-east-1 (job-b7c2), KV eviction, CPU-fallback standby. Result: queue reduced from ~2300 to ~450 and error rates dropped. Follow-ups: tenant-scoped autoscaler, long-session alerts, KV eviction tuning, CPU-fallback runbook, legal/opt-in for cross-VPC fallbacks.
